questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for the United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization?
explanation: UNESCO is correct - U-N-E-S-C-O. It stands for United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to pay close attention?
explanation: Heed is correct - H-E-E-D. To pay heed or take heed means to pay careful attention to something.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for National Aeronautics and Space Administration?
explanation: NASA is correct - N-A-S-A. NASA stands for National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of permit in past tense?
explanation: Permitted is correct - P-E-R-M-I-T-T-E-D. Double T before ED when the final consonant is doubled.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to make a serious mistake?
explanation: Blunder is correct - B-L-U-N-D-E-R. To make a blunder means to make a serious or embarrassing mistake.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus?
explanation: Scuba is correct - S-C-U-B-A. Scuba stands for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of prefer in comparative?
explanation: Preferred is correct - P-R-E-F-E-R-R-E-D. Double R before ED when stress is on the last syllable.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation used in research meaning to conduct?
explanation: Undertake is correct - U-N-D-E-R-T-A-K-E. To undertake research means to begin or carry out a research project.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for artificial intelligence?
explanation: AI is correct - A-I. AI stands for artificial intelligence the simulation of human intelligence by machines.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of begin in past tense?
explanation: Began is correct - B-E-G-A-N. Began is the irregular past tense of begin.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to take an exam?
explanation: Sit is correct - S-I-T. To sit an examination means to take a test. This is a formal British English collocation.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of omit in continuous?
explanation: Omitting is correct - O-M-I-T-T-I-N-G. Double T when adding ING to a verb ending in a single consonant after a short vowel.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for the World Health Organization?
explanation: WHO is correct - W-H-O. WHO stands for the World Health Organization.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to achieve a goal?
explanation: Accomplish is correct - A-C-C-O-M-P-L-I-S-H. Double C. To accomplish means to achieve or complete a task.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of submit in past tense?
explanation: Submitted is correct - S-U-B-M-I-T-T-E-D. Double T before ED when the final consonant is doubled.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning strong impact?
explanation: Significant is correct - S-I-G-N-I-F-I-C-A-N-T. A significant impact means a major or notable effect.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for information technology?
explanation: IT is correct - I-T. IT stands for information technology the use of computer systems to store and process information.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of travel in British English continuous?
explanation: Travelling is correct in British English - T-R-A-V-E-L-L-I-N-G. Double L before ING in British English.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning full attention?
explanation: Undivided is correct - U-N-D-I-V-I-D-E-D. To give undivided attention means to concentrate fully without distraction.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for as soon as possible?
explanation: ASAP is correct - A-S-A-P. ASAP stands for as soon as possible.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of refer in past tense?
explanation: Referred is correct - R-E-F-E-R-R-E-D. Double R before ED when stress falls on the last syllable.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning a broad variety?
explanation: Wide range is correct. A wide range is a common collocation meaning a broad variety of things.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for do it yourself?
explanation: DIY is correct - D-I-Y. DIY stands for do it yourself meaning to do home repairs or crafts without professional help.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of occur in past tense?
explanation: Occurred is correct - O-C-C-U-R-R-E-D. Double C and double R. Both consonants are doubled in inflected forms of occur.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to provide evidence?
explanation: Substantiate is correct - S-U-B-S-T-A-N-T-I-A-T-E. To substantiate a claim means to provide evidence to support it.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of cancel in British English past tense?
explanation: Cancelled is correct in British English - C-A-N-C-E-L-L-E-D. Double L before ED in British English.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to conduct research?
explanation: Undertake is correct - U-N-D-E-R-T-A-K-E. To undertake research is a standard academic collocation.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for for your information?
explanation: FYI is correct - F-Y-I. FYI stands for for your information used in emails and informal communication.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of forbid in past tense?
explanation: Forbade is correct - F-O-R-B-A-D-E. Forbade is the irregular past tense of forbid meaning to prohibit.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation used in debate meaning to present an argument?
explanation: Articulate is correct - A-R-T-I-C-U-L-A-T-E. To articulate an argument means to express it clearly and effectively.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of benefit in continuous?
explanation: Benefiting is correct - B-E-N-E-F-I-T-I-N-G. Single T. Benefit does not double the final consonant when adding ING.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to achieve a result?
explanation: Attain is correct - A-T-T-A-I-N. Double T. To attain a result means to achieve or reach a goal.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for self-regulatory organization?
explanation: SRO is correct - S-R-O. SRO stands for self-regulatory organization meaning a body that regulates itself.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of begin in present participle?
explanation: Beginning is correct - B-E-G-I-N-N-I-N-G. Double N when adding ING to a verb ending in N after a short vowel.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to form a judgment?
explanation: Assess is correct - A-S-S-E-S-S. Double S appears twice. To assess means to evaluate or form a judgment about something.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for geographic information system?
explanation: GIS is correct - G-I-S. GIS stands for geographic information system used to manage and analyze spatial data.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of commit in past tense?
explanation: Committed is correct - C-O-M-M-I-T-T-E-D. Double M and double T. Both consonants require attention.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to follow the rules?
explanation: Comply is correct - C-O-M-P-L-Y. To comply means to act in accordance with rules or requests.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of prefer in comparative?
explanation: Preferred is correct - P-R-E-F-E-R-R-E-D. Double R. The R is doubled when adding ED to a stressed final syllable.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to make a valid point?
explanation: Cogent is correct - C-O-G-E-N-T. A cogent argument is one that is clear logical and convincing.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for as soon as possible?
explanation: ASAP is correct - A-S-A-P. ASAP stands for as soon as possible and is used in informal and business communication.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of control in continuous?
explanation: Controlling is correct - C-O-N-T-R-O-L-L-I-N-G. Double L when adding ING to control.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to solve a dispute?
explanation: Arbitrate is correct - A-R-B-I-T-R-A-T-E. To arbitrate means to reach an official decision in order to settle a dispute.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning to confirm authenticity?
explanation: Authenticate is correct - A-U-T-H-E-N-T-I-C-A-T-E. To authenticate means to prove that something is genuine or valid.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of commit in progressive?
explanation: Committing is correct - C-O-M-M-I-T-T-I-N-G. Double M and double T when adding ING to commit.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning intense interest in a subject?
explanation: Fascination is correct - F-A-S-C-I-N-A-T-I-O-N. Fascination means the state of being intensely interested.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of run in past participle?
explanation: Run is correct - R-U-N. The past participle of run is run as in has run or had run.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the collocation meaning a careful examination?
explanation: Scrutiny is correct - S-C-R-U-T-I-N-Y. Scrutiny means critical observation or examination.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the inflected form of forbid in past participle?
explanation: Forbidden is correct - F-O-R-B-I-D-D-E-N. Double D before EN. Forbidden is the past participle of forbid.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the acronym for research and development?
explanation: R and D is correct. R and D stands for research and development the work done to develop new products or knowledge.
